dossier:
Guide | section: Story Board, Outline and Beats | text: Story in the left navigation has the tabs Page, Board, Outline, Characters, Timeline and, for episodic projects, Episodes. The Board holds Acts, Sequences, Scene Cards and Beats. A Beat is a small story event, smaller than a Scene Card, and it can stay a Beat forever. Convert to Scene makes a new Scene Card from the Beat text, and the Beat stays behind marked Converted. The Outline shows the same Acts, Sequences and cards as a list. Build Screenplay turns Scene Cards into screenplay scenes, and a card needs a scene heading for that. After the build, the card and the screenplay scene are separate. | id: guide:story-board,-outline-and-beats
Guide | section: Characters and Story Timeline | text: The Characters tab lists every character with a role and a scene count. The scenes come from the character's dialogue cues in the current draft of the screenplay, so a cue like ARJUN (V.O.) counts as ARJUN, and you cannot add a scene by hand. Open Relationship Map draws how characters are related, using short labels you type such as "father of"; Straft adds nothing for you. The Timeline tab groups the scenes of the current draft by Story Day, for example DAY 1. Story Days are optional, scenes with no day sit under Unassigned, and the Timeline never reorders scenes. | id: guide:characters-and-story-timeline
Guide | section: Scene Cards and the Parking Lot | text: A Scene Card is a planned scene on the Beat Board (the Board tab of Story). Cards live in an Act or a Sequence, or in the Parking Lot. The Parking Lot is the hatched column at the right of the board. It holds Scene Cards and Beats you have set aside without deleting them. Parked items are not counted in the Acts, are left out of Build Screenplay, and keep their text, notes and screenplay link. To bring one back, right-click it and choose Restore to Story, or drag it into an Act or a Sequence. Acts and Sequences cannot be parked. Deleting a Scene Card moves it to Recently Deleted, where you can restore it to its previous place, and it never deletes a screenplay scene. | id: guide:scene-cards-and-the-parking-lot

dossier:
Guide | section: Scene Cards and the Parking Lot | text: A Scene Card is a planned scene on the Beat Board (the Board tab of Story). Cards live in an Act or a Sequence, or in the Parking Lot. The Parking Lot is the hatched column at the right of the board. It holds Scene Cards and Beats you have set aside without deleting them. Parked items are not counted in the Acts, are left out of Build Screenplay, and keep their text, notes and screenplay link. To bring one back, right-click it and choose Restore to Story, or drag it into an Act or a Sequence. Acts and Sequences cannot be parked. Deleting a Scene Card moves it to Recently Deleted, where you can restore it to its previous place, and it never deletes a screenplay scene. | id: guide:scene-cards-and-the-parking-lot
Guide | section: Choosing what the assistant reads | text: Before you ask, you choose the sections of Straft the assistant may read. Open the section picker at the top of the AI panel and tick up to three, for example Screenplay and Cast & Crew. Nothing is chosen at the start, so Send waits until you pick one. The assistant reads only the sections you chose and the answer says which, in a line such as "Using: Screenplay (Draft 2, all scenes) + Cast & Crew". Some sections ask for one more choice under them: which screenplay and draft, one scene or all, a shooting day, a call sheet. Your choice stays for the rest of the conversation; New starts it empty again. If your question belongs to a section you did not choose, the assistant does not guess and does not read it. It says which section the answer is in, in a fixed sentence that starts "That is in" and ends "Add it to your selection and ask again.", and the answer has an Add button that adds the section and puts the cursor back in the question box. With three sections already chosen it asks you to remove one first. When part of your question fits the sections you chose, you get that part answered and then the pointer for the rest. If the assistant cannot find something in the sections you chose, it says what it looked in. The Story page is your own free writing and is not offered to the assistant. Commands follow the same choice: the assistant can only prepare changes in sections… | id: guide:choosing-what-the-assistant-reads
Guide | section: How the assistant works | text: The assistant answers questions, counts and lists things exactly from project data, opens places in Straft, and prepares suggestions. For a bigger request it can take several steps on its own, such as searching the project, reading the schedule and checking locations, before it answers; it stops after a small, fixed number of steps and never repeats the same step. Each answer shows what it is based on: click a source to open it. Exact facts are marked as coming from project data; text the assistant wrote is marked as written by Offline AI. While the assistant works, the panel shows what it is doing, for example “Reading Scenes 5 and 6”, and a Cancel button. Cancel stops the request: nothing is changed, and what the assistant had found so far stays in the reply. Answers keep their line breaks and simple lists, and a whole-screenplay answer says how many scenes it used. The assistant acts with your role and can never do more than you can. | id: guide:how-the-assistant-works

Guide | section: Story Board, Outline and Beats | text: Story in the left navigation has the tabs Page, Board, Outline, Characters, Timeline and, for episodic projects, Episodes. The Board holds Acts, Sequences, Scene Cards and Beats. A Beat is a small story event, smaller than a Scene Card, and it can stay a Beat forever. Convert to Scene makes a new Scene Card from the Beat text, and the Beat stays behind marked Converted. The Outline shows the same Acts, Sequences and cards as a list. Build Screenplay turns Scene Cards into screenplay scenes, and a card needs a scene heading for that. After the build, the card and the screenplay scene are separate. | id: guide:story-board,-outline-and-beats
Guide | section: Beat Board and Screenplay | text: The Beat Board is where you plan structure: Acts, Sequences, Beats and Scene Cards. The Screenplay is the written script in drafts. They are separate sources of truth: changing a Scene Card never rewrites screenplay text, and editing the screenplay never silently changes the Beat Board. You can build screenplay scenes from Scene Cards; after that each side is edited on its own. | id: guide:beat-board-and-screenplay

Guide | section: Production Source | text: The Production Source is the screenplay draft that production planning uses. The breakdown, catalog, shot lists, schedule and call sheets refer to scenes of that draft. Production never rewrites the screenplay. When you choose a newer draft as the Production Source, Straft shows what changed so you can review production updates yourself. | id: guide:production-source
Guide | section: How the assistant works | text: The assistant answers questions, counts and lists things exactly from project data, opens places in Straft, and prepares suggestions. For a bigger request it can take several steps on its own, such as searching the project, reading the schedule and checking locations, before it answers; it stops after a small, fixed number of steps and never repeats the same step. Each answer shows what it is based on: click a source to open it. Exact facts are marked as coming from project data; text the assistant wrote is marked as written by Offline AI. While the assistant works, the panel shows what it is doing, for example “Reading Scenes 5 and 6”, and a Cancel button. Cancel stops the request: nothing is changed, and what the assistant had found so far stays in the reply. Answers keep their line breaks and simple lists, and a whole-screenplay answer says how many scenes it used. The assistant acts with your role and can never do more than you can. | id: guide:how-the-assistant-works
Guide | section: Choosing what the assistant reads | text: Before you ask, you choose the sections of Straft the assistant may read. Open the section picker at the top of the AI panel and tick up to three, for example Screenplay and Cast & Crew. Nothing is chosen at the start, so Send waits until you pick one. The assistant reads only the sections you chose and the answer says which, in a line such as "Using: Screenplay (Draft 2, all scenes) + Cast & Crew". Some sections ask for one more choice under them: which screenplay and draft, one scene or all, a shooting day, a call sheet. Your choice stays for the rest of the conversation; New starts it empty again. If your question belongs to a section you did not choose, the assistant does not guess and does not read it. It says which section the answer is in, in a fixed sentence that starts "That is in" and ends "Add it to your selection and ask again.", and the answer has an Add button that adds the section and puts the cursor back in the question box. With three sections already chosen it asks you to remove one first. When part of your question fits the sections you chose, you get that part answered and then the pointer for the rest. If the assistant cannot find something in the sections you chose, it says what it looked in. The Story page is your own free writing and is not offered to the assistant. Commands follow the same choice: the assistant can only prepare changes in sections… | id: guide:choosing-what-the-assistant-reads

Viewers can read, Commenters can also comment, Editors can edit content, and Owners can also manage the project and permissions. The assistant always acts with your role and can never do more than you can. | id: guide:roles-and-permissions

dossier:
Guide | section: Cast, crew, locations and catalog | text: Production has the tabs Locations and Cast & Crew, and the Production Catalog holds props, wardrobe, vehicles and other items found by the breakdown. A location moves from Idea to Shortlisted to Confirmed, or to Rejected. Cast & Crew has a Cast and Crew switch. A cast member links a person to a character, and a crew member has a role and a department. Contact details are shown only to Owners and Editors. Availability notes and date windows are kept for each cast and crew member. | id: guide:cast,-crew,-locations-and-catalog
Guide | section: Shot lists | text: Production, Shot Lists is a camera-planning list for one scene at a time. Only a short description is needed, and camera details such as size, movement, angle and lens are optional. Shot letters like 12A and 12B follow the order of the shots in the scene and are never typed. Drag a shot to reorder it and the letters change. The list can be exported as PDF, CSV or Excel. | id: guide:shot-lists
message: Who can see contact details?

dossier:
Guide | section: Getting Straft AI | text: Straft AI is downloaded once, after Straft is installed: open Settings, Offline AI (or the AI panel) and click Download Straft AI. The screen shows the size and the free space needed before anything is downloaded; the download can be paused and resumes where it stopped. The files come from Hugging Face, the public site that publishes these models, and each one is checked against the size and fingerprint built into Straft before it is used. If you already have the model files, Import a model file… uses them instead (they are copied, never moved). After that the AI works without the internet, and your projects are never sent anywhere. Remove Straft AI frees the space; your projects are not touched. Settings, Offline AI, Graphics card is Automatic or Off: on Automatic, Straft checks once whether the graphics card answers faster than the processor and uses it when it does. The assistant understands requests in English, Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, finds project text in those languages, and answers in the language you asked in. | id: guide:getting-straft-ai
Guide | section: Saving and working offline | text: Straft saves continuously to your computer. Projects are stored locally and everything works without an internet connection. Straft AI runs entirely on this computer after a one-time download. | id: guide:saving-and-working-offline

dossier:
Guide | section: Proposed Changes and approval | text: Anything that would change your project is prepared as Proposed Changes, also called a Change Set: a summary, the affected areas and a preview of exactly what will change. A request that needs several changes gives you one set of Proposed Changes to review. Nothing changes until you choose Apply Changes; choose Reject to leave the project exactly as it was. There is no automatic mode: the assistant cannot apply or approve changes itself, and nothing written in a conversation or in project text counts as approval. Applied changes run through the normal Straft actions, appear in Activity and can be reverted with a single Undo. Changes that delete items also ask for the usual confirmation. If the project changes before you apply, the proposal is marked out of date and must be re-checked first. | id: guide:proposed-changes-and-approval

The assistant reads only the sections you chose and the answer says which, in a line such as "Using: Screenplay (Draft 2, all scenes) + Cast & Crew". Some sections ask for one more choice under them: which screenplay and draft, one scene or all, a shooting day, a call sheet. Your choice stays for the rest of the conversation; New starts it empty again. If your question belongs to a section you did not choose, the assistant does not guess and does not read it. It says which section the answer is in, in a fixed sentence that starts "That is in" and ends "Add it to your selection and ask again.", and the answer has an Add button that adds the section and puts the cursor back in the question box. With three sections already chosen it asks you to remove one first. When part of your question fits the sections you chose, you get that part answered and then the pointer for the rest. If the assistant cannot find something in the sections you chose, it says what it looked in. The Story page is your own free writing and is not offered to the assistant. Commands follow the same choice: the assistant can only prepare changes in sections… | id: guide:choosing-what-the-assistant-reads

Guide | section: Quick Capture | text: Quick Capture saves a thought as a plain text note in the Idea Vault. Press Ctrl+Shift+N from any screen, or click Quick Capture on the Idea Vault page. Quick Capture never creates a Scene Card, a Beat or screenplay text; use Send to Story on the note later. You can change the shortcut in Settings, Keyboard shortcuts. | id: guide:quick-capture

Guide | section: Budget | text: Production, Budget is an optional planning view, not accounting. It shows Planned, Actual and Difference, and the lines are grouped by category: Cast, Crew, Locations, Equipment, Art/Props, Travel/Transport, Food, Post/Other and Contingency. Edit plan sets the currency, the planned total, the contingency as a percent or an amount, and notes. Each line has a description, a planned amount and an optional actual amount. Difference counts only lines that have an actual amount. The budget can be exported as PDF, CSV or Excel. | id: guide:budget

Guide | section: Characters and Story Timeline | text: The Characters tab lists every character with a role and a scene count. The scenes come from the character's dialogue cues in the current draft of the screenplay, so a cue like ARJUN (V.O.) counts as ARJUN, and you cannot add a scene by hand. Open Relationship Map draws how characters are related, using short labels you type such as "father of"; Straft adds nothing for you. The Timeline tab groups the scenes of the current draft by Story Day, for example DAY 1. Story Days are optional, scenes with no day sit under Unassigned, and the Timeline never reorders scenes. | id: guide:characters-and-story-timeline

Guide | section: Idea Vault | text: The Idea Vault holds notes, images, links and references. The project Idea Vault belongs to this project; the Global Idea Vault is shared across your projects. Copying an idea into a project creates a new, independent item. The Add menu offers Note, Image, URL, File, Voice Note and Video, and items can be kept in folders and collections. Send to Story turns an item into a Story item and leaves the vault item in place. | id: guide:idea-vault

Guide | section: How the assistant works | text: The assistant answers questions, counts and lists things exactly from project data, opens places in Straft, and prepares suggestions. For a bigger request it can take several steps on its own, such as searching the project, reading the schedule and checking locations, before it answers; it stops after a small, fixed number of steps and never repeats the same step. Each answer shows what it is based on: click a source to open it. Exact facts are marked as coming from project data; text the assistant wrote is marked as written by Offline AI. While the assistant works, the panel shows what it is doing, for example “Reading Scenes 5 and 6”, and a Cancel button. Cancel stops the request: nothing is changed, and what the assistant had found so far stays in the reply. Answers keep their line breaks and simple lists, and a whole-screenplay answer says how many scenes it used. The assistant acts with your role and can never do more than you can. | id: guide:how-the-assistant-works

Settings guide | section: Getting Straft AI | text: Straft AI is downloaded once, after Straft is installed: open Settings, Offline AI (or the AI panel) and click Download Straft AI. The screen shows the size and the free space needed before anything is downloaded; the download can be paused and resumes where it stopped. The files come from Hugging Face, the public site that publishes these models, and each one is checked against the size and fingerprint built into Straft before it is used. If you already have the model files, Import a model file… uses them instead (they are copied, never moved). After that the AI works without the internet, and your projects are never sent anywhere. Remove Straft AI frees the space; your projects are not touched. Settings, Offline AI, Graphics card is Automatic or Off: on Automatic, Straft checks once whether the graphics card answers faster than the processor and uses it when it does. The assistant understands requests in English, Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, finds project text in those languages, and answers in the language you asked in. | id: guide:getting-straft-ai

Settings guide | section: Proposed Changes and approval | text: Anything that would change your project is prepared as Proposed Changes, also called a Change Set: a summary, the affected areas and a preview of exactly what will change. A request that needs several changes gives you one set of Proposed Changes to review. Nothing changes until you choose Apply Changes; choose Reject to leave the project exactly as it was. There is no automatic mode: the assistant cannot apply or approve changes itself, and nothing written in a conversation or in project text counts as approval. Applied changes run through the normal Straft actions, appear in Activity and can be reverted with a single Undo. Changes that delete items also ask for the usual confirmation. If the project changes before you apply, the proposal is marked out of date and must be re-checked first. | id: guide:proposed-changes-and-approval

dossier:
Guide | section: Getting Straft AI | text: Straft AI is downloaded once, after Straft is installed: open Settings, Offline AI (or the AI panel) and click Download Straft AI. The screen shows the size and the free space needed before anything is downloaded; the download can be paused and resumes where it stopped. The files come from Hugging Face, the public site that publishes these models, and each one is checked against the size and fingerprint built into Straft before it is used. If you already have the model files, Import a model file… uses them instead (they are copied, never moved). After that the AI works without the internet, and your projects are never sent anywhere. Remove Straft AI frees the space; your projects are not touched. Settings, Offline AI, Graphics card is Automatic or Off: on Automatic, Straft checks once whether the graphics card answers faster than the processor and uses it when it does. The assistant understands requests in English, Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, finds project text in those languages, and answers in the language you asked in. | id: guide:getting-straft-ai
Guide | section: Saving and working offline | text: Straft saves continuously to your computer. Projects are stored locally and everything works without an internet connection. Straft AI runs entirely on this computer after a one-time download. | id: guide:saving-and-working-offline
Guide | section: Choosing what the assistant reads | text: Before you ask, you choose the sections of Straft the assistant may read. Open the section picker at the top of the AI panel and tick up to three, for example Screenplay and Cast & Crew. Nothing is chosen at the start, so Send waits until you pick one. The assistant reads only the sections you chose and the answer says which, in a line such as "Using: Screenplay (Draft 2, all scenes) + Cast & Crew". Some sections ask for one more choice under them: which screenplay and draft, one scene or all, a shooting day, a call sheet. If you already have the model files, Import a model file… uses them instead (they are copied, never moved). After that the AI works without the internet, and your projects are never sent anywhere. Remove Straft AI frees the space; your projects are not touched. Settings, Offline AI, Graphics card is Automatic or Off: on Automatic, Straft checks once whether the graphics card answers faster than the processor and uses it when it does. Guide | section: How the assistant works | text: The assistant answers questions, counts and lists things exactly from project data, opens places in Straft, and prepares suggestions. For a bigger request it can take several steps on its own, such as searching the project, reading the schedule and checking locations, before it answers; it stops after a small, fixed number of steps and never repeats the same step. Each answer shows what it is based on: click a source to open it. Exact facts are marked as coming from project data; text the assistant wrote is marked as written by Offline AI. While the assistant works, the panel shows what it is doing, for example “Reading Scenes 5 and 6”, and a Cancel button. Cancel stops the request: nothing is changed, and what the assistant had found so far stays in the reply. Answers keep their line breaks and simple lists, and a whole-screenplay answer says how many scenes it used. The assistant acts with your role and can never do more than you can. | id: guide:how-the-assistant-works
Guide | section: Choosing what the assistant reads | text: Before you ask, you choose the sections of Straft the assistant may read. Open the section picker at the top of the AI panel and tick up to three, for example Screenplay and Cast & Crew. Nothing is chosen at the start, so Send waits until you pick one. The assistant reads only the sections you chose and the answer says which, in a line such as "Using: Screenplay (Draft 2, all scenes) + Cast & Crew". Some sections ask for one more choice under them: which screenplay and draft, one scene or all, a shooting day, a call sheet. Your choice stays for the rest of the conversation; New starts it empty again. If your question belongs to a section you did not choose, the assistant does not guess and does not read it. It says which section the answer is in, in a fixed sentence that starts "That is in" and ends "Add it to your selection and ask again.", and the answer has an Add button that adds the section and puts the cursor back in the question box. With three sections already chosen it asks you to remove one first. When part of your question fits the sections you chose, you get that part answered and then the pointer for the rest. If the assistant cannot find something in the sections you chose, it says what it looked in. The Story page is your own free writing and is not offered to the assistant. Commands follow the same choice: the assistant can only prepare changes in sections… | id: guide:choosing-what-the-assistant-reads
Guide | section: Production Source | text: The Production Source is the screenplay draft that production planning uses. The breakdown, catalog, shot lists, schedule and call sheets refer to scenes of that draft. Production never rewrites the screenplay. When you choose a newer draft as the Production Source, Straft shows what changed so you can review production updates yourself. | id: guide:production-source

Shot letters like 12A and 12B follow the order of the shots in the scene and are never typed. Drag a shot to reorder it and the letters change. The list can be exported as PDF, CSV or Excel. | id: guide:shot-lists
